speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what is the Ministry's assessment of the casino-related crime situation in Singapore since the casinos commenced operations in 2010; and (b) what steps are taken to ensure that casino-related crime in Singapore will be kept in check.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police exchange information with their counterparts in other countries on the latest casino-related crime trends and persons of interest.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police and CRA also work closely with the casino operators to deter crime through regular surveillance and patrols.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: And what can we do to deter these syndicates, particularly the foreign crime syndicates, from coming over to Singapore and ensnaring Singaporeans as well?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He has a particular worry that organised crimes, especially by foreign syndicates, will enter Singapore through casinos.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Actually, the number that relates to organised crime groups is very few.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Among all the offences, theft and cheating account for the most.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For the theft-related cases, they mostly involved theft of gambling chips belonging to other patrons at the game tables.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, this is not quite the behaviour of organised crime syndicates.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Other common scenarios include theft of cash, valuables, unattended bags and wallets from patrons.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, there is a pattern and these types of theft offences are not representative of organised crimes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The cheating-related cases usually involve the past posting of bets.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In other words, the outcome of the game is revealed and some of the patrons decide to try their luck, in case the croupier was not paying attention.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They would place a bet on a location which would suggest that they won but, in fact, they did not.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, such cases also are one of the more common ones.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There have also been cases where counterfeit chips were used by patrons.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But the Member's concerns are very well noted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will continue to keep a close eye.
